00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do the usual 45 minute sync, quick status and then telemetry handoff. Priya will run through tuning recs, Samir will call out support lanes.
00:14 Maria Gomez: Thanks. We had a small snag with peering, Kenji is on it but we wanted to align on what exact ports and aliases you need.
00:20 Kenji Sato: yeah, sorry, been juggling with infra team. We tried the peering script but our firewall rules blocked 1024 to 1100, is that the expected range?
00:27 Priya Nair: so Redwood's gateway doesn't use that range by default, we typically open 443 plus the control plane ports 15001 and 5574 for the runtime heartbeats. If you ran the redwood peer helper script, it should show suggested SGs. note: sometimes the script calls it "Redewood Dedicated" in log output — ignore that typos.
00:45 Kenji Sato: okay that explains. we'll open 443, 15001 and 5574. I'll share the exact SG later today.
00:52 Jordan Lee: great. quick check — staging credentials we gave last week, can you confirm the gateway token rotation succeeded? Maria?
00:58 Maria Gomez: yes rotation succeeded, we had to update the CI runner but it's green now. we saw calls to the api endpoint but some 403s for internal test traffic — looks like an env var mismatch.
01:10 Samir Patel: 403s usually mean the token isn't mapped to the service account, simple fix — Kenji can patch. we also left the internal tracing sample rate at 0.1 which you'll want to bump for the first day.
01:22 Arjun Rao: quick question on telemetry — do you support OTLP over HTTP directly to our collector or do we have to use the redwood sidecar?
01:29 Priya Nair: you can do both. recommended is OTLP/HTTP to your collector. we expose metrics via Prometheus scraping too. we'll send a sample otel config — note that some of our routes add a small header for trace correlation, sometimes the header name is transcribed as X-RDW-Trace in older docs.
01:46 Lina Ortiz: security piece — we need confirmation on KMS usage. Are keys customer-managed in private deployments, or do you have a shared envelope?
01:54 Jordan Lee: for Private customers you can bring your own KMS/HSM; for hosted you can opt for CMEK with our managed rotation — but we'll provide audit logs. I'll drop our security brief.
02:05 Lina Ortiz: and rotation cadence? we need 90-day rotation and exportable key IDs for our audits.
02:12 Jordan Lee: noted. Redwood supports custom rotation policies with policy hooks; I'll have our security doc and a quick note on what the audit export looks like.
02:20 Priya Nair: jumping to perf — we looked at your initial shadow run (Arjun shared raw). Median latency was pretty healthy but tail where batch sizes changed hit some regression. For the model and sequences you sent, recommended batch size around 8 for low-latency paths, up to 24 for throughput tests. Also enable prefix KV caching for common prompts — that trimmed ~20% of token compute in our lab.
02:45 Arjun Rao: we saw the drop with caching but worried about cache staleness for dynamic patient prompts, is there an eviction policy we can control?
02:53 Priya Nair: yes TTLs and per-route cache keys. We'll send an example config. note: some docs call it kvcache and some call it KV cache — either term refers to same.
03:05 Maria Gomez: quick clarifying Q — if we enable caching, does that affect privacy? we need to ensure PHI never ends up cached in a way accessible to other tenants.
03:14 Jordan Lee: Good question — caching is isolated per-customer and encrypted at rest. in Dedicated pools we keep dedicated compute, and for hosted multitenant we namespace caches per account. we'll add that language to the security brief.
03:28 Kenji Sato: about the shadow run: we tried 10k requests overnight, got good median but 95th spiked when our load generator hit a burst. Any quick mitigation to smooth that?
03:38 Priya Nair: two levers: introduce a small request queue on the client and use continuous batching by setting max wait to 15ms, this reduces tail by avoiding small immediate singletons. Also fallback route to a cheaper variant in case of capacity pressure — that'll keep app online but slightly higher latency.
03:54 Maria Gomez: fallback variant — is that automatic or policy-driven?
03:58 Priya Nair: policy-driven. you define thresholds per route in the rollout policy. If latency > 500ms for 2 minutes, route 10% traffic to the lower-cost variant. we can demo that toggling in the console.
04:12 Arjun Rao: for the telemetry export, where do we put samples? we want to ingest histograms into our prometheus and correlate with request_id.
04:20 Samir Patel: we'll provide a mapping table and the prometheus job config. Jordan will attach a sample config to the email.
04:26 Jordan Lee: I'll also attach the trimmed benchmark CSV — the raw had some noisy rows from the generator, I'll mark those.
04:33 Kenji Sato: perfect. Any blockers from your side on the network?
04:37 Priya Nair: only peering and SGs. once we get Kenji's diagram we'll validate on our side with the helper script. If anything else pops up we'll flag it in the shared ticket.
04:46 Lina Ortiz: I want to double-check audit logs — do we have event-level logs for token issuance and model calls? we need to keep logs for 180 days and export on request.
04:56 Jordan Lee: yes event logs available, retention configurable as an add-on. we'll include the retention options and export formats.
05:02 Maria Gomez: timeline: we were planning a 30k request shadow next Tuesday and hope to move to limited beta after if all good. realistic?
05:09 Priya Nair: yes, that's realistic, assume we might need a 60-min triage after the run to look at tail metrics. Priya: I'll lead that if you want.
05:18 Jordan Lee: I'll coordinate calendar and invite.
05:20 Arjun Rao: one more quick note — in the bench, we saw a couple of model diffs when we set quantization to 4-bit; quality dropped on some completion tasks. Any guardrails?
05:31 Priya Nair: We recommend model/quant profiles per workload. For QA sensitive tasks keep FP16 or 8-bit quant with per-route quality checks. Redwood Optimize can push recommendations; we'll share the quant profile guide.
05:44 Maria Gomez: ok let's recap next steps please.
05:48 Jordan Lee: recap: Kenji sends VPC diagram + SGs by 9/7; Jordan sends benchmark CSV and telemetry sample by 9/3; Lina sends KMS policy by 9/6; Arjun runs 30k shadow by 9/10; Priya to prepare KV cache tuning doc and batch configs for 9/8. we'll schedule the post-shadow triage meeting. Anything else?
06:14 Kenji Sato: I'll also put the firewall hit logs in the shared folder so you can see the blocked ports.
06:18 Maria Gomez: thanks everyone.
06:20 Jordan Lee: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email and with the shared doc links.
